consensus_summary: All three blind responses converge on the pearl as symbolizing the kingdom of heaven (or salvation/Christ/the gospel) as a treasure of supreme worth, based chiefly on Matthew 13:45-46, with standard alternatives: the reversed reading (Christ as merchant, church/believer as pearl), pearls as sacred truth not to be profaned (Matt 7:6), the New Jerusalem's pearl gates (Rev 21:21), pearls as worldly luxury (1 Tim 2:9; Rev 17-18), and a minor wisdom-comparison strand (Job 28:18).
book_summary: The book identifies the pearl as 'the one complete light' — reading the Hebrew peninim (KJV 'rubies') as pearls, so wisdom and the virtuous bride are priced above pearls; and identifying the night sky's 'one pearl' as the full moon (via keseh, 'fulness/time appointed,' wordplay with 'throne'), governor of the appointed times, with the one-pearl gates of the city read as the merchant's entry at the King's gate.
consensus_core_identification: Pearl = the kingdom of heaven / salvation as the object of supreme value, worth surrendering everything to obtain (with a recognized reversed reading making the church/believer the pearl purchased by Christ).
book_core_identification: Pearl = the full moon as the one complete light governing the appointed times, with wisdom/the bride valued above pearls (peninim) and the one-pearl gates as lunar/calendrical entry imagery.
boundary_disagreement: The book relocates the pearl's referent from the kingdom-of-heaven/valuation theme to a celestial-calendrical object (the full moon) and to wisdom/the bride via the peninim lexical claim. It reclassifies Rev 21:21's pearl gates from heavenly glory into moon/appointed-time symbolism, and imports verses no consensus response associates with pearls at all (Ps 81:3; Prov 7:20; Job 26:9; Ps 104:19).
material_contradiction: None asserted outright: the book records the common teaching (kingdom of heaven, or church purchased by Christ) in its common-view note without explicitly denying it, and its wisdom-above-pearls strand loosely echoes a minority alternative (Job 28 wisdom comparisons). But the full-moon identification appears in no consensus response or alternative.
rationale: The book's central identification — the pearl as the full moon, the 'one complete light' governing appointed times, established through Hebrew wordplay (peninim/keseh/kisseh) — is absent from the mainstream consensus and from every listed alternative. It does not merely narrow or extend the kingdom-of-heaven reading; it introduces a new referent built on a lexical-astronomical chain no blind response anticipates. Because the book does not explicitly contradict the consensus (it acknowledges the common teaching as 'commonly taught' rather than false, and its wisdom strand partially overlaps a minority alternative), this is novelty by absence rather than replacement-by-contradiction, making NOVEL the correct verdict over DIVERGENT.
strongest_objection: One could argue for DIVERGENT rather than NOVEL: by presenting the full moon as the pearl's true identification and demoting the kingdom/church reading to a 'commonly taught' note, the book functionally replaces the consensus referent — Rev 21:21's gates become lunar imagery rather than heavenly glory, which sits uneasily with the consensus use of that same verse. Alternatively, one could argue the wisdom-above-pearls strand (Prov 3:15; 31:10) sufficiently matches the minority wisdom alternative in Responses B and C to count as REFINED.
